samples.summary: canUndo/canRedo read-only guard is asserted against an empty history, so the assertions hold with or without the new guard
samples.evidence: The new test 'lets no write reach the store on a read-only mount' (editor.test.ts:36-63) builds `new MemNoteStore('hello')` and never seeds an undo unit. `MemNoteStore.canUndo()/canRedo()` (store/memory.ts:189-195) return false on empty stacks, so `expect(api.canUndo()).toBe(false)` / `toBe(false)` at lines 58-59 pass identically whether the diff's `canUndo: () => !readOnly && store.canUndo()` (editor.ts:661-662) guard exists or not. The existing test at editor.test.ts:223 shows the seeding idiom (`store.editText(5,5,'!')` before `initialize(..., true)`) that would have made these assertions discriminating.

samples.summary: The read-only undo/redo refusal is only exercised with an empty store history, so the damaging case (a viewer reverting real content) is not covered
samples.evidence: editor.test.ts:51-57 calls `api.undo()/api.redo()` on a store with no recorded unit. Without `if (readOnly) return` in `runHistory` (editor.ts:340) the calls would reach `store.undo()`, which pops nothing and returns null — so `expect(api.getText()).toBe('hello')` and `expect(store.getText()).toBe('hello')` are vacuous for this path; only the `expect(undo).not.toHaveBeenCalled()` spy assertion discriminates. The scenario that actually loses data (a store carrying an undoable unit, as at editor.test.ts:228) is untested through the API.

samples.summary: The newly added `EditorState.readOnly.of(readOnly)` layer has no test that would fail if it were removed
samples.evidence: The diff adds two independent read-only enforcement layers (`EditorState.readOnly` facet and the `changeFilter`). The new tests only observe the outcome (document/store unchanged), which the changeFilter alone produces, so deleting `EditorState.readOnly.of(readOnly)` — the facet that makes @codemirror/commands, autocomplete and the vim keymap decline rather than mutate — leaves the whole notes suite green. No test asserts a command *returns false* / declines on a read-only mount.

samples.summary: Remote-change test captures the last `subscribeRemote` listener rather than noteSync's specifically
samples.evidence: editor.test.ts:69-79 overwrites `emit` on every `subscribeRemote` call, so it emits into whichever subscriber registered last. It currently happens to be noteSync (the assertion at line 81 would fail otherwise), but the test is coupled to subscription order; a future subscriber added after noteSync would turn this into a confusing failure rather than a clear one.
